**Tracking:** Meticulous record-keeping is key. Use a simple spreadsheet or a free budgeting app to track *all* income and expenses throughout the year. Categorize everything – W-2 income, freelance income, deductible expenses (like charitable donations or business expenses if applicable), and any potential tax credits you might be eligible for. Don't rely on memory; document everything.

**Setting Aside Money:** Aim to set aside a fixed percentage of each paycheck, ideally 15-20%, into a dedicated savings account specifically for taxes. Since you prefer low risk, a high-yield savings account is a good choice – it's safe and earns a bit of interest. Automate this transfer so it happens without you having to think about it.

**Avoiding Surprises:** Early in the year, estimate your tax liability based on your previous year's return and any anticipated changes in income or deductions. Review this estimate quarterly and adjust your savings accordingly. Consider making estimated tax payments throughout the year (if you have significant income not subject to withholding) to avoid penalties at tax time. Finally, consult IRS publications or a tax professional for clarification on any complex tax rules or situations.
